title: collector.json - per-target metadata and state
description: One file per vendor-product target at vendors/<vendor>/<product>/collector.json. Written by the collector agent and the scheduler runtime; read-only for the generated fetch script. Sections: identity (who/what), build (what was built, from which inputs), state (what the runner must remember between runs), health (is it working), repair (only while being fixed), recent_runs (history), alerts (what a human should see).

target.description: <vendor slug>/<product slug>, e.g. cisco/nx-os. Equals the folder path under vendors/.

status.description: active: scheduled and healthy. broken: self-heal exhausted its 3 attempts, human needed. repairing: an agent repair is in progress (see `repair`). disabled: a human switched it off; never scheduled.

builder_version.description: The advisory-script-builder skill `version` the product script was built with. Older than the skill's current version -> stale -> rebuilt with reason spec_changed.

study.description: The source_study.json the script was built from. Differs from the file on disk -> rebuilt with reason study_changed.

registry_hash.description: SHA-256 of the target's registry entry at build time. Differs from a fresh hash -> rebuilt with reason registry_changed.

validated_at.description: When the last --dry-run --limit 5 passed the agent's thresholds.

last_dry_run_stats.description: The stats block of the dry run that passed at `validated_at`. Baseline for the regression guard (version_kind_mix drift) and for the failure_report.stats on a repair.

source_fingerprint.description: Structural fingerprint of the listing and a sample detail page (e.g. hashes of selector paths, content type, pagination shape) recorded at build time. A changed fingerprint at run time is the self-heal trigger; the old and new values become failure_report.fingerprint_diff.

state.description: Everything the runner must remember between runs. Written by the runtime from the script's RUN_SUMMARY; the script itself only reads it. Any map left out is treated as empty.

cursor.description: Resume point passed as --since on the next run. null = next run is a full backfill. Only advances on exit code 0.

last_full_listing.description: When the listing was last scanned end to end (no --since pruning). The daily full scan that catches old incomplete advisories keys on this.

failed.description: Advisories we tried to download and do not have. Keyed by advisory_id. Retried by detail URL on every run until gave_up.

status.description: Last HTTP status; 0 when no response was received or the failure was not HTTP (parse error, affects_product() returned None).

reason.description: Short classification: timeout, connection, http_5xx, http_403, parse_error, affects_product_unreadable, csaf_unreadable, ...

gave_up.description: Set by the agent when its give-up policy (attempts and/or age since first_failed) is met. Never fetched again.

incomplete.description: Stored advisories missing an important field (workaround, cve_ids, version_affected, security_details) or their CSAF twin. Keyed by advisory_id. Re-fetched when the listing row updates, or every 7 days for sources without row dates.

rejected.description: Advisories fetched but not stored. Keyed by advisory_id. A product-mismatch ID rests 30 days or until its listing row updates - unless audit.verdict is wrong, then it is fetched again next run. `audit` is written by the collector agent only.

reason.description: product mismatch | date_published missing | schema invalid | ...

detail.description: The affects_product() detail, e.g. 'primary: IOS XE only; text: no affected-products section'.

withdrawn.description: Stored advisories that have stopped appearing in the listing. Keyed by advisory_id. missing_runs counts consecutive full-listing scans without the ID; confirmed_at is set once the vendor's page itself says withdrawn (is_withdrawn()). The record stays in advisories.json either way.

health.description: Is the target working right now. Updated by the runtime after every run; read by the scheduler and the agent's monitoring pass.

consecutive_failures.description: Runs with exit code 2 in a row. Reset to 0 on exit 0 or 1.

source_available.description: false after a listing_unreachable run; the scheduler backs off instead of hammering the source.

records_last_24h.description: New + updated records in the last 24 h, maintained by the runtime. Zero for an unusual stretch is the 'source went quiet' signal.

schedule_next.description: When the scheduler intends to run next (after backoff).

repair.description: Present only while status is repairing. Holds the agent's retry budget so a crashed repair resumes at the right attempt. Deleted when status returns to active or becomes broken.

trigger.description: validation: a dry run fell below thresholds. self-heal: a scheduled run failed or the source fingerprint changed.

last_report.description: The failure_report (builder skill section 2.3) passed on the most recent attempt.

manifest.description: Optional cached summary of advisories.json so dashboards and the agent need not open the data file.

recent_runs.description: Newest first. One entry per non-dry run, built by the runtime from the script's RUN_SUMMARY and exit code. The agent reads rejected[] for its audit and log for http_evidence on a repair; the runtime reads the last 30 as its anomaly baseline.

status.description: Runtime-assigned: exit 0/1/2/3 -> success/partial/failed/config_error; timeout when the 30-minute wall clock stopped the run (cursor unmoved, not a failure).

backfill.description: true when the run started with a null cursor (first backfill in progress); excluded from anomaly baselines.

population.description: Fraction of this run's stored records with each field populated, e.g. {"summary":1.0,"version_affected":0.95,"date_published":1.0}. Anomaly baseline input.

log.description: Repo-relative path of the run's log file.

alerts.description: Open alerts for a human, keyed by alert code (e.g. coverage_gap, broken, source_quiet, rejections_to_audit). Removing the key clears the alert.
